sections.text:
1 Est liber Masallae (cf. p. 87, n. 3) De receptione planetarum a Iohanne Hispa-
lensi versus et Venetiis a. 1493 editus; cf. Steinschneider, p. 379 c.
2 Liber de interrogationibus editus est Venetiis cum Introductorio eiusdem
auctoris (supra, p. 92, n. 2) ; cf. Steinschneider, Hebraïsche Uebersetzungen des
Mittelalters, p. 601.
3 Liber exstat in nonnullis codicibus sed auctor qui Gergis, Jergis, Zergius, etc,.
vocatur, ignotus est; cf. Steinschneider, l. c., p. 370, § 22. 4 An idem ac Sergius de
Rešain Syriacus celeberrimus scriptorum Graecorum interpres? , [Boll]. Cf. Duval,
Littérat. syriaque, p. 254 s., 365 s. — In editione L(ugdunensi) pro “ Gergis „ legitur
“ Regum „ et Liber regum de significatione Planetarum in duodecim domibus caeli,
incipiens Sol cum fuerit in ascendente, invenitur apud Thaddaeum Hagecium ab
Hagek, Astrologica opuscula antiqua, Pragae, 1564 (Quaternio F).
4 Hoc spectat ad librum Masallae (supra, n. 1) De interpretationibus cuius ini-
tium tantum latine editum est. — Liber de cogitationibus, in editione Veneta
incipit verbis De cogitationibus ab intentione refertur et praecipit Messahala ;
cf. Steinschneider, l. c., p. 379 f, g.
5 Liber Zahelis De significatione temporum, incipiens verbis allatis, editus est
cum eius Introductorio ; cf. supra n. 2.
6 Liber Novem Iudicum iam supra memoratur (p. 92, n. 6). Liber III Iudicum
Steinschneidero non innotuit, sed exstat in codicibus Liber VII Iudicum (l. c.,
p. 394, § 51).
7 Cf. supra, p. 92, n. 3 et 4.
sections.en:
1 It is the book of Masalla (cf. p. 87, n. 3) On the Reception of the Planets translated by John of
Seville and published at Venice in 1493; cf. Steinschneider, p. 379 c.
2 The Book on Interrogations was published at Venice with the Introductory of the same
author (above, p. 92, n. 2) ; cf. Steinschneider, Hebraïsche Uebersetzungen des
Mittelalters, p. 601.
3 The book exists in some codices but the author who is called Gergis, Jergis, Zergius, etc.,
is unknown; cf. Steinschneider, l. c., p. 370, § 22. 4 Is it the same as Sergius of
Reshaina the Syrian, the most famous interpreter of Greek writers? , [Boll]. Cf. Duval,
Littérat. syriaque, p. 254 f., 365 f. — In the L(yons) edition for “ Gergis „ is read
“ Regum „ and the Book of Kings on the Signification of the Planets in the Twelve Houses of Heaven,
beginning When the Sun is in the ascendant, is found in Thaddaeus Hagecius ab
Hagek, Astrologica opuscula antiqua, Prague, 1564 (Quaternio F).
4 This refers to the book of Masalla (above, n. 1) On Interpretations of which only the
beginning has been published in Latin. — The Book on Thoughts, in the Venice edition
begins with the words On thoughts is referred from intention and Messahala commands ;
cf. Steinschneider, l. c., p. 379 f, g.
5 The book of Zahel On the Signification of Times, beginning with the words cited, was published
with his Introductory ; cf. above n. 2.
6 The Book of the Nine Judges is already mentioned above (p. 92, n. 6). The Book of the Three Judges
was not known to Steinschneider, but there exists in codices the Book of the Seven Judges (l. c.,
p. 394, § 51).
7 Cf. above, p. 92, n. 3 and 4.

summary.headline: Astrological Works and Judges
summary.text: Bibliographic list of astrological works by Messahallah, Zahel, and Gergis, including books on planetary receptions, interrogations, planetary significations in the houses, hidden things, thought, and time. It also cites the Books of the Nine and Three Judges and treatises of Aristotle and Ptolemy addressed to Aristoxenus.
